metaDescription: Five compact cordless chainsaws at or under $200, including RYOBI ONE+ pruners and a Greenworks 40V 12-inch, compared on platforms, bars and batteries.
expertTake: The Greenworks 40V 12-inch is the best overall buy for an owner who wants a saw on a real battery platform, with parts and a warranty behind it. The RYOBI 18V pruning saw is the pick for anyone already holding ONE+ batteries. Buyers who cut firewood regularly should look past this band to a 16-inch saw.
introParagraphs: At this budget the choice is less about the saw and more about the battery it runs on. Platform saws share packs with drills and trimmers, which changes the real cost of ownership.
You are also choosing between a compact pruner and a true 12-inch limbing saw. Prices move, and the $200 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12-Inch Cordless Chainsaw 2.0Ah
products.description:
This is the only 40V saw in the group, and voltage is why it behaves differently from the 20V imports. Higher voltage lets the motor draw less current for the same power, so it holds speed in a cut and runs cooler. A 12-inch bar then gives it the reach to cut limbs and small logs rather than just branches.

The maker claims about 50 cuts through 4x4 treated lumber per charge, which is a more useful run time statement than a wattage number because it describes real work. The 2.0Ah pack is modest, though, so it suits trimming and limbing rather than a full afternoon of bucking. Compared with the Seesii and FXAFXA, which offer 4.0Ah packs, it stores less energy but puts it into a stronger platform.

Ownership is the best argument: a mainstream brand, a 40V pack that powers mowers, trimmers and blowers, and widely stocked chains and bars. Keep it oiled, check chain tension, and store the pack indoors. It is a sensible saw for a homeowner who wants one battery system across the yard. A practical habit is to keep a short log of which wood you cut, since resinous pine gums the bar and fresh oak dulls the chain faster, and both change how often you must clean the saw.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a saw on a shared 40V platform.
pros: Forty-volt platform shares batteries with yard tools
Twelve-inch bar handles limbs and small logs
Run time stated as real cuts

products.name: RYOBI HP 18V Brushless 6-Inch Compact Pruning Chainsaw Kit
products.description:
This RYOBI sits on the ONE+ HP system, which claims faster cutting when paired with the right battery. A brushless motor and a 6-inch bar make it a precision pruner rather than a limbing saw, and the compact body suits one-handed placement on a branch you can see.

The ONE+ platform is among the largest in home tools, which means a battery you already own may fit. The listing is bulk packaged, so check exactly what ships, since the battery and charger may differ from a retail kit.

Compared with the Greenworks 12-inch, it cuts less but handles better in tight places. Keep the chain oiled and sharp and store the battery indoors. It is a good add-on for someone already invested in ONE+. Treat the first few uses as a break-in period, checking chain tension, oil level and the lock switch each time. A bulk-packaged kit can arrive without a manual, so look up the model's instructions online before cutting. The ONE+ system also includes tools such as trimmers and blowers, so a battery bought for this saw can serve the rest of the yard. That flexibility is the reason owners tolerate the smaller bar.
products.bestFor: ONE+ owners wanting a compact pruner.
pros: Part of the large ONE+ battery family
cons: Bulk packaging means contents need checking

products.name: RYOBI 18V Brushless 8-Inch Compact Pruning Chainsaw Tool Only

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Tool only, battery and charger sold separately

products.description:
The 8-inch RYOBI is sold as a tool only, so a battery and charger must be bought separately if you do not own them. That is the key fact for budgeting, because the pack is the most expensive part of a cordless saw.

The 8-inch bar cuts thicker limbs than the 6-inch pruner, and the brushless motor and compact body keep it manageable. For a ONE+ owner it is a cheap and capable addition.

If you have no ONE+ batteries, price the full setup before deciding. Keep the chain oiled and sharp. Because there is no battery in the box, add the pack and charger to your budget before you decide, and match the pack to your other tools. A larger pack gives more cuts but adds weight on a saw you hold at arm's length. Because the tool is bare, do not judge it by the lowest price alone, and compare it against the HP kit and the Greenworks as complete setups.
products.bestFor: ONE+ owners who need only the tool.
pros: Eight-inch bar on the ONE+ platform
Uses batteries you may already own

products.name: Seesii 12-Inch Brushless Cordless Chainsaw 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The Seesii gives you two 4.0Ah packs and an automatic oiler in the box, so everything needed to start cutting ships with the saw. The packs store more energy than the Greenworks's single 2.0Ah cell, but the voltage class is lower, so torque in hardwood is limited.

The 1200W label is a peak claim and cannot be compared with the Greenworks's cut-count statement. Think of it as a capable limbing saw for softwood and brush.

Compared with the platform saws, you give up shared batteries and brand support, and gain a complete kit. Keep the chain sharp and the reservoir filled. Because two 4.0Ah packs are included, you can charge one while you cut, which makes this the easiest way to finish a long limbing job without stopping. Rotate the packs so they age evenly, and store them partly charged. Compared with the Greenworks, it trades platform support for larger packs and the oiler, which suits someone who wants to start cutting today and not think about batteries again.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a complete kit with large packs.
pros: Two 4.0Ah packs and a charger included

products.name: FXAFXA 12-Inch 20V Brushless Cordless Chainsaw 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The FXAFXA is the budget route to a 12-inch bar, with two 4.0Ah packs and a brushless motor. Its horsepower claim is a peak figure on a 20V platform.

It is a good limbing saw for softwood but will struggle with seasoned hardwood.

Keep it oiled and sharp. Replacement chains for 12-inch saws are cheap, so buy a spare with the saw and swap when the cutters dull, instead of forcing a blunt chain through wood. Its brushless motor means less heat on long limbs, but it still needs breaks, and the packs should rest before charging.  Use it for limbing softwood and brush and keep the bar clear of dirt.
products.bestFor: Budget limbing of softwood and brush.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Greenworks 40V and RYOBI 18V ONE+ saws run on batteries that power other tools. The Seesii and FXAFXA come with packs that only fit those saws. A platform changes total cost the moment you own a second tool. Weigh the cost of a battery and charger against the saw, because on tool-only listings they can double the total.

The RYOBI 8-inch is tool only, and the RYOBI HP kit is bulk packaged. A battery and charger can cost as much as the saw. Always check the box contents. If you already own a drill from a platform, compare the saw's battery against it before buying any pack.

Six inches for shrubs, eight for thicker limbs, twelve for small logs. Longer bars need more power and carry more kickback. Choose the shortest bar that does the job. A saw with a chain brake is safer on a bigger bar, so check the listing for one.

The Greenworks claims about 50 cuts in treated 4x4 lumber, which is more meaningful than wattage. Compare packs by real work where the maker offers it. Think about how the saw will be stored; a bar cover and a hook in the garage protect both you and the chain.

A 40V saw holds speed under load better than a 20V one. For hardwood and thick limbs, voltage matters more than a bigger claimed horsepower. Watch for kickback: never cut with the tip of the bar, and keep your body out of the line of the bar.

Look for a chain brake or guard and a lock switch. Wear glasses, gloves and sturdy boots, and avoid cutting above shoulder height. A spare chain is the cheapest upgrade you can make, so buy one with the saw.

specDecoder.meaning: A maker statement of real work, such as about 50 cuts in 4x4 lumber. Compare saws by real work done, not by peak figures.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks gives one; the imports give wattage instead.

specDecoder.meaning: The battery system voltage, such as 18V ONE+ or 40V. This decides whether you buy a battery at all.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 40V pack does not fit an 18V tool.

specDecoder.meaning: The listing excludes the battery and charger. Make sure the listing says whether a battery is included.
specDecoder.watchFor: The RYOBI 8-inch is sold this way.

specDecoder.meaning: A peak figure such as 2.56 hp. It can matter more than the claimed horsepower in thick wood.
A motor without brushes, cooler and more efficient. Everything here is brushless, so use other specs to separate them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform strength
howWeEvaluated.description: We graded the battery family behind each saw. Greenworks 40V and RYOBI ONE+ led. Standalone kits scored lower for long-term value. Platform strength mattered most because the battery drives long-term cost and convenience. We also asked how each saw would feel after a full afternoon of limbing, not just at the first cut.

howWeEvaluated.title: Box contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether a battery and charger ship. The tool-only RYOBI and bulk-packaged HP kit were flagged. Listings that hid the battery status were marked down until we could read the box contents. Honest labeling of what is in the box was a requirement for a high score.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cut capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bar length to likely jobs. The 12-inch saws led for capacity. A longer bar was credited only when it came with enough battery to use it. Where a listing was bulk packaged, we recommended checking the contents before purchase.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claim realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We discounted horsepower and wattage figures. A stated cut count was treated as more useful. Where makers gave cut counts, we preferred them to wattage numbers. Run time statements in cuts earned extra credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted guards and warranties. Owner feedback patterns informed the durability view. Support and warranty were weighed for the branded options. Owner feedback patterns on chain stretch and oiler clogging shaped the maintenance notes.

cards.label: Platform saw
cards.text: The Greenworks and RYOBI saws share batteries with other tools, ease parts and warranty issues, and lower the cost of a second tool.

cards.label: Standalone kit
cards.text: The Seesii and FXAFXA include big packs and an oiler, but the batteries fit nothing else.

howToChoose.note: Pick a platform if you own or plan tools from that family; pick a kit for a one-off saw.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 12-inch bar, a platform battery with spares and a sharp chain. Storm wood is dirty and dulls chains quickly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V is the best fit, with the Seesii as the big-pack alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut firewood or fell small trees. A 16-inch saw on a 40V or 56V platform with a chain brake sits above this cap.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only prune. A compact RYOBI or the FXAFXA covers it.

maintenance.why: A dry chain overheats and dulls. Keep the bar cover on the saw when it is not in use, even indoors.
A slack chain can jump the bar. Blow sawdust out of the chain brake area if one is fitted.
Dull chains burn wood and strain the motor. Wipe resin off the bar with a rag and solvent made for the job.

faq.q: Is a platform saw better than an import kit?
faq.a: For long-term cost, usually. A shared battery lowers the cost of every extra tool and parts are easy to find. Platform choice is usually the largest long-term cost factor.

faq.q: Do I need to buy a battery for the RYOBI 8-inch?
faq.a: Yes if you do not own ONE+ packs. The listing is tool only. Check the listing carefully before you pay.
Small softwood logs, yes. Regular firewood work is better done with a 16-inch saw. Use a spare chain and sharpen the dull one later.

faq.q: Is a 12-inch bar safe to use one-handed?
faq.a: No. Use two hands, eye protection and gloves, and keep the chain sharp. A glove and eye protection are not optional.
Expect fade after several seasons. Store them indoors at part charge. Keep a spare pack if you plan a big cleanup.
